method: Page fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Every claim is verbatim-checked against that file with scripts/verify.py. Prose paraphrases; source_text stays verbatim. The antibiotic table and the stepped allergic rhinitis regimens are tables rendered as text, quoted as contiguous blocks; column alignment is a transcription risk and must be confirmed against the page before prescribing. Cefalexin, ceftriaxone/metronidazole and montelukast are named without doses in the source and no dose is reconstructed.

claims.claim: Infective rhinosinusitis rarely causes orbital or intracranial complications
claims.source_text: Infective rhinosinusitis rarely leads to orbital or intracranial complications

claims.claim: Allergic rhinitis managed with allergen minimisation, antihistamines and nasal steroids
claims.source_text: Allergic rhinitis should be managed with allergen minimisation, antihistamines +/- nasal steroids

claims.claim: Neonatal rhinitis is common and often self-resolving
claims.source_text: Neonatal rhinitis is common and often resolves without treatment

claims.claim: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis definitions and classification
claims.source_text: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis are characterised by inflammation of the nasal mucosa and paranasal sinuses, respectively (often co-exist) … Rhinitis is classified as allergic (perennial or seasonal) or non-allergic

claims.claim: Rhinosinusitis time classification
claims.source_text: Recurrent acute: At least 3 acute episodes with at least 10 days or more with no symptoms in 6 months, or at least 4 episodes in 12 months … Subacute: 4-12 weeks … Chronic: >12 weeks

claims.claim: Viral cause predominates with bacterial secondary infection after 10 days
claims.source_text: Acute rhinosinusitis is most commonly caused by viral infections, but secondary acute bacterial rhinosinusitis may develop, particularly if symptoms persist beyond 10 days

claims.claim: Viral and bacterial organisms
claims.source_text: Viral: Rhinovirus, RSV, influenza, adenovirus, additional systemic symptoms of viral illness common … Bacterial: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (non-typeable), Moraxella catarrhalis

claims.claim: Allergic rhinitis and asthma relationship
claims.source_text: Significant implications for childhood asthma … A risk factor for the development of asthma … Affects asthma control … Impacts the prognosis and progression of asthma into adulthood

claims.claim: The pig nose manoeuvre
claims.source_text: Use the 'pig nose' manoeuvre to examine the nasal mucosa (tilt child's head back, elevate the nasal tip with your thumb, and illuminate the orifice with light/otoscope) … Examine mucosal surfaces, colour and calibre of turbinates, and position of septum

claims.claim: Mucosal appearance distinguishes allergic from infective
claims.source_text: Pale, boggy mucosa of inferior turbinates is in keeping with allergic rhinitis … Red and oedematous mucosa is seen more commonly in infective or medication induced rhinitis

claims.claim: Allergic facies signs
claims.source_text: Allergic facies (Dennie-Morgan lines, allergic salute, allergic shiners, transverse nasal crease and mouth breathing)

claims.claim: Acute bacterial sinusitis history including purulence caveat
claims.source_text: Preceding viral illness is common … Persistent nasal discharge >10 days (purulence is of little significance) … Maxillary toothache … Unilateral facial pain

claims.claim: Otitis media signs reflect shared aetiology
claims.source_text: Signs of acute otitis media are commonly seen, reflecting a shared aetiology

claims.claim: Complications of acute bacterial sinusitis
claims.source_text: Periorbital and orbital cellulitis … Cerebral abscess … Cavernous sinus thrombosis … Meningitis … Encephalitis … Subdural and epidural empyema

claims.claim: Watchful waiting for 3 days before antibiotics
claims.source_text: Consider watchful waiting for 3 days to assess for spontaneous resolution as acute viral sinusitis is the most likely cause with similar signs and symptoms … Antibiotics can be commenced if there is no improvement at this time or if there is clinical worsening

claims.claim: Antibiotic regimen table for acute bacterial sinusitis
claims.source_text: 1st line Amoxicillin 15 mg/kg (max 500 mg) oral tds for 5 days (Cefalexin if penicillin allergy) If not improving, Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 22.5 mg/kg (max 875 mg) oral 12 hourly for another 5 days Systemically unwell or unable to tolerate oral Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 25 mg/kg (max 1 g) IV 6 hourly (Ceftriaxone and metronidazole if penicillin allergy)

claims.claim: Nasal swabs should not be taken
claims.source_text: Nasal swabs should not be taken. Culture is not indicative of sinus pathogens and is therefore not helpful

claims.claim: Steroid sprays decongestants and antihistamines have no benefit in acute sinusitis
claims.source_text: Steroid sprays, decongestants, or antihistamines has been shown to have no benefit in acute sinusitis

claims.claim: Surgery rarely needed in acute bacterial sinusitis
claims.source_text: Surgery is very rarely needed for acute bacterial sinusitis (in the absence of orbital or intracranial complications)

claims.claim: CT indications
claims.source_text: CT is the imaging modality of choice, consider if … Failed medical management … Possible orbital or intracranial complication … Surgery is being considered

claims.claim: Chronic rhinosinusitis is uncommon under 12 and defined at 12 weeks
claims.source_text: Symptoms occur for 12 weeks or more … Nasal obstruction/congestion … Postnasal drip … Loss of smell … Halitosis

claims.claim: Chronic rhinosinusitis risk factors
claims.source_text: Exposure to cigarette smoke … Adenoid hypertrophy … Reflux disease … Cystic fibrosis … Mucociliary impairment … Immune deficiency … Prolonged use of intranasal decongestants

claims.claim: Chronic rhinosinusitis saline and steroid regimen
claims.source_text: Intranasal saline spray or irrigation for minimum 6 weeks … Sodium chloride, 2 sprays or irrigations into each nostril twice daily and as required … Use prior to steroid spray … Intranasal corticosteroid for minimum 6 weeks

claims.claim: No role for decongestants
claims.source_text: There is no role for oral or intranasal decongestants

claims.claim: Assess adherence and technique and refer to ENT if unsuccessful
claims.source_text: Assess treatment adherence and nasal spray technique … Referral to ENT is recommended if the above are unsuccessful in relieving symptoms

claims.claim: Allergic rhinitis stepped approach principles
claims.source_text: To be used in conjunction with allergen minimisation for common allergens eg house dust mite, pollens, pet dander and mould … Trial each step for around 4 weeks before assessing response … Assess treatment adherence and nasal spray technique before escalating … Use minimal effective regimen

claims.claim: Step 1 antihistamine either route but not both
claims.source_text: Step 1: Oral antihistamine OR intranasal antihistamine … Using both is not of additional benefit … Can be used as required for intermittent symptoms or regularly for persistent symptoms

claims.claim: Oral versus intranasal antihistamine properties
claims.source_text: More effective than intranasal for symptoms such as itch at non nasal sites … Typically better tolerated in younger children … Less sedating antihistamines recommended … More effective than oral for local nasal symptoms … Faster onset of action … Require good technique

claims.claim: Cetirizine paediatric dosing
claims.source_text: Eg cetirizine … 1-2 years, oral drops, 2.5 mg (5 drops) twice daily … 2-6 years, oral 5 mg once daily or 2.5 mg twice daily … 6-12 years, oral 10 mg once daily or 5 mg twice daily … 12-18 years, oral 10 mg

claims.claim: Azelastine nasal spray dosing
claims.source_text: Eg azelastine (1mg/mL nasal spray) … 5 years, 1 spray into each nostril twice daily

claims.claim: Step 2 intranasal corticosteroid with mometasone dosing
claims.source_text: Step 2: Add intranasal corticosteroid … Especially effective for nasal obstruction and reduces ocular symptoms … Symptom relief usually starts within a few days but a minimum trial of 4 weeks of consistent use is required to establish efficacy … Eg mometasone 50 microg nasal spray … 2-12 years, 1 spray into each nostril daily … 12-18 years, 2 sprays into each nostril daily. Reduce to 1 spray into each nostril daily when symptoms controlled

claims.claim: Step 3 combination spray and cease oral antihistamine
claims.source_text: Step 3: Consider change to combination intranasal antihistamine and corticosteroid if predominant nasal symptoms … Cease any oral antihistamine if taking … Eg azelastine with fluticasone propionate 125/50 microg nasal spray … 6-18 years, 1 spray into each nostril twice daily

claims.claim: Step 4 eye drops and montelukast
claims.source_text: Ocular symptoms: add eye drops … Ketotifen 0.025% eye drops - 3-18 years, 1 eye drop twice daily … Olopatadine 0.1% eye drops - 3-18 years, 1 eye drop twice daily up to 14 weeks … Intermittent allergic rhinitis and co-existing asthma, consider adding montelukast

claims.claim: Immunotherapy criteria duration and cost
claims.source_text: For moderate to severe symptoms not responding to treatment (including allergen minimisation) … Subcutaneous (SCIT) or sublingual (SLIT) for at least 3 years … Not covered by PBS and there may be a significant yearly cost

claims.claim: Neonatal rhinitis treatment
claims.source_text: Nasal antihistamines, decongestants, steroids and humidifiers are not recommended … Saline drops can be used prior to feeding … Specialist review if impacting breathing or feeding

claims.claim: Other causes of rhinitis
claims.source_text: Foreign body: Unilateral symptoms, brown discharge, foreign body may be visible, foul odour common from the affected nostril … Association with menstrual cycle, pregnancy … Subclinical hypothyroidism in older children … Typically aspirin and other NSAIDS … Consider 'rebound congestion' (inflammation of the nasal mucosa caused by overuse of topical nasal decongestants) if history suggestive

claims.claim: Vasomotor rhinitis features
claims.source_text: Sudden onset and offset of watery nasal discharge. Can be triggered by strong smells or changes in environmental temperature

claims.claim: Rarer causes if recurrent or severe
claims.source_text: Anatomical anomalies … Immunodeficiency … Ciliary dysfunction … Cystic fibrosis

claims.claim: Diagnosis is clinical and testing only confirms sensitisation
claims.source_text: In most instances the diagnosis is made clinically and no investigations are required … Further testing is not diagnostic and needs to be correlated with clinical history. Positive results only confirm sensitisation to allergens … Testing may assist with allergen minimisation

claims.claim: Serum specific IgE versus skin prick testing
claims.source_text: Serum specific IgE (previously known as RAST) to environmental allergens. Not affected by anti-allergy medications … Skin prick testing. Affected by anti-allergy medications

claims.claim: Paediatric consultation and ENT referral triggers
claims.source_text: All systemically unwell children … Suspected orbital or intracranial complication … Suppurative complications are present, or surgical intervention may be required … Medically refractory nasal obstruction

claims.claim: Immunology referral triggers
claims.source_text: Further allergy testing and interpretation is required to facilitate allergen minimisation … Severe or inadequately controlled allergic rhinitis despite treatment … Consideration for allergen immunotherapy

claims.claim: Transfer criteria
claims.source_text: Suspected intracranial involvement with altered conscious state, seizures or focal neurological signs

claims.claim: Brand cost and accessibility vary
claims.source_text: There are many different brands of pharmacotherapy treatments available with varying cost and accessibility (over the counter or script)
